title: Millimeter-Sized 0.1pM LoD Wireless 16-Channel Organic-Electrochemical-Transistor-Based Electrochemical Sensing SoC
problem: Miniaturized electrochemical sensor implants for long-term biomarker monitoring face challenges in achieving high sensitivity, wide dynamic range, and spatial resolution while remaining small enough for implantation; traditional three-electrode (3E) systems and ISFETs suffer from low scalability and limited channel integration.
motivation: Chronic disease management (autoimmune, cardiovascular, cancer) requires continuous monitoring of inflammatory cytokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6); miniaturized wireless implant systems enable less-invasive long-term monitoring.
method: The system packs 16 organic electrochemical transistors (OECTs—devices that detect biomarkers by responding to chemical binding) onto a millimeter-sized chip and sends measurements wirelessly, replacing older three-electrode and ion-selective field-effect transistor designs that could only handle one or two channels. The circuit interface between each OECT and the measurement system is optimized to manage the high idle current these transistors demand.
key_novelty: A millimeter-sized wireless chip integrates 16 organic electrochemical transistors (devices that detect biomarkers by changing electrical conductivity) to achieve 0.1 picomolar sensitivity—the ability to measure 0.1 trillionths of a mole per liter.
contributions: Optimized sensor interface managing OECT power consumption
primary_theme: Miniature OECT-based wireless biomarker sensing SoC
